channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Former Bishkek Deputy Appeals to President Sadyr Japarov Over Mandate Issue
item.description: Former Bishkek City Kenesh deputy Zhanybek Asanbekov has again appealed to President Sadyr Japarov regarding his deputy mandate. Asanbekov stated that three months after the president's initial instruction, the issue remains unresolved. He previously claimed he resigned under duress and intended to challenge the decision.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Criticizes Jalal-Abad Regional Leadership for Unresolved Citizen Issues
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov expressed dissatisfaction with the performance of Jalal-Abad regional leaders and law enforcement, citing years of unresolved citizen problems. He demanded immediate action on land and property disputes and an end to delays in addressing appeals, following numerous complaints from local residents.

item.title: Putin Calls Claims of Ukraine Losing Territory Inappropriate
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that claims of Ukraine losing territory are inappropriate, asserting that these lands historically belong to Russia. He referenced the results of the 2022 referendums held in occupied Ukrainian territories, which are not recognized internationally. Putin made these remarks following discussions with US envoy Steve Whitcoff.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Proposes Reducing Court Case Review Periods
item.description: Kyrgyz lawmakers have proposed a bill to shorten the timeframes for reviewing court cases. The initiative aims to expedite judicial decisions and prevent lengthy legal processes. Proposed changes include reducing deadlines for wage disputes and health damage claims, expanding video conferencing options, and limiting session postponements. Court chairmen would be obligated to monitor and enforce these deadlines.

item.title: First Human Case of Shamoonda Virus Confirmed in Kazakhstan
item.description: The World Health Organization confirmed the first documented human case of the Shamoonda virus, previously only found in animals. The patient, who had immunosuppression, died. The virus was first detected in cows in eastern France in June, causing significant drops in milk yield. It has since spread to thousands of farms in Germany.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Meat Exports Decline in January-August 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan's meat exports decreased by 6.6% to 69,000 tons in January-August 2026, despite stable production. Revenue from foreign sales fell to $262.4 million. Poultry and turkey exports saw the largest drop, while beef exports increased by 6.2%, with Uzbekistan remaining the primary buyer. Russia and Kyrgyzstan increased purchases of pork.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Woman Posing as 'Wildberries Queen' Sentenced for Fraud
item.description: A Kazakh court has sentenced Altynai Didarkyzy, who presented herself as the 'Wildberries Queen' on social media, for defrauding 35 people. She promised high returns on investments in the Russian marketplace, with total damages exceeding $1 million. Victims, many of whom were single mothers, invested sums ranging from 500,000 to 50 million tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Ruble and Euro Rise, Yuan Hits Record High; Tenge Also Appreciates
item.description: The Chinese yuan reached a new historical record against the Kyrgyz som for the sixth consecutive day. The Russian ruble continued its strengthening trend, hitting a new October high. The Kazakh tenge and the euro also saw appreciation, while the US dollar remained largely stable. These trends are reflected in the official rates from the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and exchange bureaus.

item.title: President Awards State Honors Ahead of Republic Day
item.description: Ahead of Republic Day, the President has awarded state honors to a group of citizens for their significant contributions to social, economic, cultural, and spiritual development, and for strengthening inter-ethnic friendship and cooperation. Awards included the 'Hero of Labor of Kazakhstan' title for smelter Abdurashit Dospanov.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Stop Summoning School Principals to Meetings, Official Says
item.description: Uzbekistan will cease summoning school principals to meetings, announced Erkinjon Turdimov, the Minister of Preschool and School Education, during a meeting in Samarkand. The ministry also plans to review the licensing procedures for private educational institutions. This initiative aims to reduce administrative burdens on school leadership.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Allows Awarding Top Ranks Without Prior Service
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan can now award top civil service ranks without meeting standard experience requirements or special commission review. This change, amending a 2016 decree, allows for exceptions based on significant professional achievements for individuals in political and special positions. Educational and service year requirements are also adjusted for certain roles.

item.title: International Volunteers Convene in Kyzylorda for Aral Sea Environmental Week
item.description: An international volunteer week, 'Green Aral: Volunteers For Life 2026,' is underway in Kyzylorda to protect the Aral Sea's nature and ecosystem. Over 100 volunteers from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and 10 regions of Kazakhstan are participating, alongside local students and activists.

item.title: Kazakh President Awards 'Hero of Labor' Title to Metallurgist
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has awarded the title 'Hero of Labor of Kazakhstan' to Abdurashit Dospanov, a metallurgist at the Zhezkazgan copper smelting plant. The award recognizes his outstanding production achievements and significant contributions to the plant's continuous operation. Dospanov has a 45-year career in the industry.

item.title: US Senator: Ukraine Would Not Exist Without American Aid
item.description: Senator Marco Rubio stated that Ukraine would not exist without US assistance. He also commented that for the war with Russia to end, both sides must make concessions. The US Secretary of State's remarks were also mentioned in relation to ending the conflict.

item.title: Over 50,000 People Died in European Cities Due to Heat This Summer, Study Finds
item.description: A study published in Nature Health reports that over 50,391 people died in European cities due to heat this summer, with over 32,600 deaths linked to climate change. Researchers noted that summer 2026 was likely the worst on record for heat-related mortality in Europe. The continent is warming faster than any other.

item.title: Samarkand Declaration Adopted at Global Summit on Child Well-being
item.description: The 'Investing in Our Children' global summit concluded in Samarkand with the adoption of the Samarkand Declaration. The document emphasizes the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the 'Leave No One Behind' principle, acknowledging children's vulnerability to crises like climate change and conflict, and reaffirming parental responsibility supported by the state.

item.title: Tashkent Considers Municipal Bonds to Fund Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Tashkent city administration and US investment bank Oppenheimer & Co. are discussing the possibility of issuing municipal bonds to finance infrastructure projects. The parties explored prospects for Tashkent's entry into international capital markets and the development of public-private partnerships. The agreement aims to expand Tashkent's relations with international financial institutions and investors.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Visits Kashkadarya Region to Review Reforms
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Kashkadarya region on October 21-22 to assess socio-economic reforms. He noted the region's transformation and set a goal to eliminate poverty and unemployment by year-end. Growth in industry, services, and agriculture was observed, but further development of value-added products and resource utilization is needed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims for 80% Digital Oversight of Energy Resources by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy is implementing the Digital Qazaqstan strategy to achieve 80% digital oversight of energy resources by 2028. This initiative involves monitoring fuel sales facilities and improving data accuracy, automated transfer, and system integration. Target coverage is set at 20% by 2026 and 60% by 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan President and OSCE PA Chair Outline New Cooperation Directions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with OSCE Parliamentary Assembly Chairman Pedro Agramunt to discuss expanding cooperation. They noted positive interaction dynamics, including participation in election observation and dialogue on ecology, migration, and transport. A joint roadmap for new cooperation priorities was agreed upon.

item.title: Turkmenistan Institute Marks 30 Years of Democracy and Human Rights Studies
item.description: The Institute of State, Law, and Democracy of Turkmenistan celebrates its 30th anniversary. The institute, established to strengthen democratic institutions and ensure constitutional rights, focuses on scientific research in human rights and freedoms. Turkmenistan emphasizes developing state-society relations based on law and individual freedom.

item.title: New Oilseed Plant to Be Constructed in Turkmenistan's Dashoguz Region
item.description: Turkmenistan's President has signed a decree for the construction of a new oilseed processing plant in the Garashsyzlyk district of Dashoguz region. The plant will have an annual capacity to process 60,000 tons of industrial cotton seeds. This initiative aims to develop the agricultural sector and ensure food security.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Eurasian Economic Commission Chairman
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Bakytzhan Sagintayev, Chairman of the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC). They noted the expanding cooperation between Uzbekistan and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), with growing trade and investment. Uzbekistan participates in EAEU programs on trade digitalization and climate. A new cooperation plan aims to reduce trade barriers.

item.title: Iran Reports Attack on Seven Oil Tankers in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran announced that seven oil tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels sustained damage from potential strikes by Tehran or mine explosions. This incident has heightened concerns about a renewed conflict in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Developing New Approaches to Natural Risk Assessment and Ecosystem Restoration
item.description: Uzbekistan is hosting an international conference on applying systems analysis to assess natural disaster risks and adapt to climate change. Experts from 12 countries are participating. The event is organized by the Russian Academy of Sciences, the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan, and UNIDO.

item.title: Kazakhstan Supports UAE Candidate for UN Secretary-General Position
item.description: Kazakhstan has backed the UAE's initiative to nominate Lana Zaki Nusseibeh, UAE Minister of State, for the position of UN Secretary-General. Kazakhstan believes that increasing the number of candidates will facilitate consensus, though disagreements within the UN Security Council complicate the election process.

item.title: Has the World Grown Accustomed to the Crisis in Afghanistan?
item.description: Afghanistan's crisis, once a top global foreign policy issue, now receives diminished attention despite ongoing poverty, hunger, and social restrictions. The world's fading focus shifts the crisis from an emergency to a chronic problem, potentially normalizing the suffering of millions.

item.title: Astana to Open New Medical Facilities by Year-End, Mayor Kasymbek Announces
item.description: Astana Mayor Zhenis Kasymbek announced that several new medical facilities will open in the capital by the end of the year. These include a diagnostic complex at City Hospital No. 2 and a pediatric trauma center. Further facilities, like a perinatal center and polyclinics, will be implemented in phases.

item.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Visits Uzbekistan for C5+1 Meeting in Samarkand
item.description: The visit of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to Uzbekistan and the C5+1 ministerial meeting in Samarkand mark a significant step in bilateral and regional cooperation. The visit is crucial for strengthening political dialogue, expanding economic ties, and deepening engagement in regional security and sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China Discuss Investment Projects in Agriculture and Employment
item.description: Officials in Uzbekistan's Syrdarya region met with Zhang Guijun, Executive Director of Haid International Holdings Limited, to discuss deepening cooperation in fish and poultry farming. They also explored expanding production, increasing agricultural output, and implementing advanced technologies to boost employment. The company is currently developing a 92-hectare fish farming project and investors proposed an additional 200 hectares for expansion.

item.title: New Polyclinic Opens in North Kazakhstan, Serving Over 40,000 Residents
item.description: A new polyclinic, built at a cost of 5.1 billion tenge, has been completed in Beskol village, North Kazakhstan region. It is designed for 250 patient visits per shift and will begin full operations in 2027 after equipment installation and licensing. The facility will serve over 40,000 residents of the Kyzylzhar district, enhancing local access to medical services.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Mark 1050th Anniversary of Physician Abu Ali ibn Sino in 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan will widely celebrate the 1050th anniversary of the birth of the great physician and scholar Abu Ali ibn Sino (Avicenna) in 2030. The government approved a roadmap on October 19 for studying and promoting his scientific heritage. A research center dedicated to Ibn Sino will be established at Bukhara State Medical Institute.

item.title: US Pentagon May Use Heat Ray Against Migrants at Mexico Border
item.description: The US Pentagon has authorized the Department of Homeland Security to test a directed-energy weapon, described as a heat ray, for seven months. The invisible electromagnetic waves can penetrate human skin, causing a burning sensation to deter individuals. This testing is intended for use at the Mexico border.

item.title: Astana to Open New Diagnostic Complex and Trauma Center
item.description: Astana is expanding its medical infrastructure with new facilities, including a diagnostic complex at City Hospital No. 2 and a pediatric trauma center at City Children's Hospital No. 2. The diagnostic complex will serve residents of the left bank, offering various services and accommodating up to 900 patients daily. Additional facilities like a perinatal center and clinics are also planned.

item.title: Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, and Uzbekistan Expand Humanitarian Dialogue
item.description: A trilateral meeting in Ashgabat focused on strengthening neighborly relations based on shared history and culture. Discussions included climate resilience, Turkmenistan's National Forest Program, a regional climate technology center, and environmental education for youth. The Azerbaijani and Uzbek delegations expressed gratitude for Turkmenistan's hospitality.

item.title: Italy and Spain to Fully Abolish Border Checks After Ceuta Events
item.description: Italy and Spain have agreed to cease extending Schengen border checks following the crisis in Ceuta. While border controls will be lifted, both nations will enhance information exchange to ensure security within the Schengen area. The temporary suspension had affected freedom of movement for two and a half months after Italy initially imposed controls on August 1st.

item.title: UN Experts Express Concern Over Deportation of Afghan Refugees from Europe
item.description: UN experts have expressed grave concern over reports of Afghan refugees being deported from EU member states and returned to Afghanistan. They warned against actions normalizing relations with the Taliban and emphasized the principle of non-refoulement, citing the dire human rights situation in Afghanistan, including potential crimes against humanity.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Impose Financial Sanctions for Water Use Violations Starting 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will implement financial sanctions against legal entities violating water usage regulations. First-time offenders will receive an initial warning under certain conditions. Those who pay half of the fine within a month will be exempt from the remaining amount.

item.title: Bishkek and Manas Join Central Asian Coalition of Sustainable Cities
item.description: Bishkek and Manas have joined the Central Asian Coalition of Sustainable Cities, expanding its membership from five to ten cities. The coalition, founded in 2025, aims to facilitate experience exchange and practical solutions for urban resilience against floods, earthquakes, and other threats, while integrating climate risks into long-term development planning.

item.title: UN Secretary-General Calls for Global End to Conflicts and Respect for International Law
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged an end to escalating global conflicts, emphasizing the critical need to respect international law. He highlighted that wars are intensifying and spreading, fueling further violence. Guterres called for the protection of civilians, freedom of navigation, and the use of diplomacy to achieve peaceful resolutions.
